processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Cast ingot of Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C (prepared by vacuum induction melting) homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h before hot forging.
Hot forged between 1200 and 900 °C ensuring more than 60% deformation with intermediate heating, then cooled by water quenching.

Forged material solutionized at 1050 °C for 1 h and water quenched to retain maximum austenite phase. This is the parent process (proc_solutionized-wq-1050c-1h) that yields the MAF-0 state before MAF.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 33% normal strain in a single pass (equivalent strain ≈ 0.47)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Warm MAF along three mutually perpendicular directions (one pass) on a 100-ton hydraulic press; 30×20×20 mm billet in a die with groove 32×20 mm; sample and die heated to 250 °C and soaked for two hours; ram speed 1 mm/s; samples lubricated with MoS2 before pressing. The 1-pass condition is denoted MAF-1.

structures.overall_structure: Warm multiaxially forged (1 pass) Fe-30Mn-9Al-0.8 C low-density steel: single-phase (majority austenite) FCC microstructure that is deformed and progressively subdivided, with a markedly increased dislocation density and changed preferred orientation relative to the solution-treated state.

microstructure_list.region: Central analysed plate of the MAFed billet (location shown in Fig. 3a); normal/pressing direction probed by XRD/EBSD

phases_present.morphology: deformed, elongated grains; grain subdivision with dense low-angle subgrain network
phases_present.grain_size: 35 μm average (EBSD); average crystallite size 13.4 nm (XRD)
phases_present.texture: changed from (111) in solutionized state to (220) preferred orientation; texture being broken up/randomized; many different crystallographic directions parallel to pressing direction

phases_present.morphology: carbide reflections κ(220) and κ(222) present; unchanged before and after MAF

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: Initial (MAF-0) distribution was relatively wide; after deformation the distribution becomes narrower/more uniform; MAF-1 area-fraction vs grain-size curve sits between MAF-0 and MAF-3.
grain_structure.texture: Solution-treated material was strongly textured with normal direction parallel to [101]; after 1 pass texture is randomized/broken up with many directions parallel to pressing direction.

phase_interfaces.coherence: grain boundaries characterized by misorientation angle; high-angle boundary (15°–180°) fraction 0.292, low-angle boundary (1°–15°) fraction 0.708

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dislocation accumulation at low-angle subgrain/grain boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: After 1 pass the low-angle boundary fraction increases drastically to 0.708 (from 0.367 in MAF-0) while the high-angle fraction falls to 0.292; a dense green low-angle subgrain network forms inside grains, reflecting heavy dislocation accumulation and subgrain subdivision.

interfaces.slip_behavior: No deformation twinning occurs in this alloy; deformation proceeds by dislocation glide/accumulation (KAM average increases to 0.72°), with dislocation mobility and annihilation at grain boundaries suppressed at low temperature.
interfaces.phase_evolution: No new phase forms during MAF; carbide reflections remain unchanged (no change in precipitation), and the strong initial texture progressively randomizes with pass number.
interfaces.interface_notes: A negligible annealing twin boundary fraction of 0.007 is present in MAF-1. Grain boundary character in MAF-1 (Fig. 7b): low-angle 1°–15° = 0.708, high-angle 15°–180° = 0.292.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Miniature round tensile specimen cut from the MAF-1 billet: gauge length 16 mm, overall length 26.5 mm, gauge Ø4 mm, shoulder Ø7.2 mm, fillet radius R1; two specimens per pass for reliability.
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tested on an INSTRON hydraulic universal testing machine. Elastic length subtracted from elongation data; reported plastic length used for plastic strain.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress–strain curve for MAF-1 shown in Fig. 10 (red curve); starts between 1000 and 1200 MPa, rises to a maximum between 1200 and 1400 MPa at strain ≈0.25, fractures near strain 0.3.

strain_hardening_rate.note: amount of work hardening for MAF-1 (decreases from 392 MPa in MAF-0)

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Decomposition of yield-strength increase relative to solution-annealed MAF-0 (measured YS).

yield_strength.note: Measured YS of MAF-1; increase of 531 MPa attributed to dislocation-density difference and 129 MPa to grain refinement relative to MAF-0.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: On MAF for 1 pass the yield strength increases drastically, i.e. by three times, to 1040 MPa (from 380 MPa for solutionized MAF-0); UTS increases to 1368 MPa (from 762 MPa); total elongation decreases from 75% to 30%; work-hardening amount decreases from 392 MPa to 328 MPa.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Scan speed 2°/min, step size 0.02°, 2θ range 40°–120°; electro-polished samples; instrumental peak broadening (from standard silicon) subtracted. Peak broadening analysed by Williamson–Hall plot.
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine phase constitution, crystallite size, lattice microstrain and dislocation density of MAF-1.
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-1 XRD (Fig. 5): two dominant sharp peaks near 51° and 87° 2θ (γ(220) tallest) plus weak δ(211) and κ(222) features near 95–105° 2θ; intensity change from (111) in solutionized sample to (220) of MAF-1 indicates texturing. Avg. crystallite size = 13.4 nm, avg. microstrain = 5.18 × 10^-3, dislocation density = 5.57 × 10^15 m^-2; Burgers vector b = 0.259 nm.

characterization_methods.technique: Electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD), including image-quality maps, inverse pole figure (IPF) maps and Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) maps
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Electro-polished samples; grain boundaries located with misorientation >15° (equivalent grain size method); 60 μm scale bar in EBSD maps.
characterization_methods.purpose: Quantify grain size, grain-boundary misorientation fractions, crystallographic texture and local misorientation (stored strain) of MAF-1.
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-1: average grain size 35 μm; high-angle (15°–180°) boundary fraction 0.292, low-angle (1°–15°) fraction 0.708; IPF map shows many differently oriented deformed/elongated grains (texture breaking up); average KAM value 0.72°.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10^-3 s^-1; miniature round specimens (gauge 16 mm, Ø4 mm gauge, Ø7.2 mm shoulder); two specimens per pass.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength and elongation of MAF-1 (and all MAF passes).
characterization_methods.key_findings: MAF-1: YS = 1040 MPa, UTS = 1368 MPa, total elongation 30%, work-hardening amount 328 MPa.

characterization_methods.technique: Combustion infrared detection analysis and wet chemical analysis
characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: LECO CS744 analyzer (carbon); wet chemical analysis (other elements)
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine the actual chemical composition after solutionization.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Actual composition after solutionization is Fe-30.6Mn-9.1Al-0.79 C.

computational_details.simulation_method: 3-D finite element analysis (explicit dynamics) of the MAF forging operation, incorporating the modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model
computational_details.software_used: ABAQUS/Explicit with a user-material VUMAT subroutine
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Modified Johnson-Cook constitutive model (Eq. 6) with strain-dependent dislocation density (Eq. 7) and grain size (Eq. 8); J-C model parameters from the authors' previous study and Table 4.
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 3-D model 30 mm × 20 mm × 20 mm; die and punch discrete rigid bodies, workpiece deformable; mesh size 0.6 mm (41382 C3D8R hex elements, reduced integration with hourglass control); punch displacement 10 mm in Y (height); die fixed; material flow allowed only in X (flow direction) and constrained in Z by the die wall; friction coefficient 0.15; steady-state MAF simulated by mapping deformation fields from previous passes.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Simulated dislocation density, grain size and flow stress compared with XRD (Fig. 5) and EBSD (Fig. 8) measurements at the Fig. 3(a) location. For MAF-1 the FE-simulated yield strength (dashed curve, Fig. 13) lies just below the experimental value (1040 MPa). Simulation predicted maximum central-region strain ≈0.6 after one pass, exceeding the applied external strain value of 0.46, in an X-shaped deformation pattern.

analytical_models.equation_role: Predicts flow stress incorporating grain-boundary strengthening (Hall-Petch) and dislocation (Taylor) strengthening added to the original J-C strain/strain-rate/thermal terms.
analytical_models.model_note: Eq. 6: σflow = (σ0 + k(df^-1/2 − d0^-1/2) + αMGb(ρf^1/2 − ρ0^1/2) + Bε^n)[1 + C ln(ε̇/ε̇0)][1 − ((T−Tr)/(Tm−Tr))^m]. Implemented via VUMAT with six state-dependent variables (SDV1–SDV6).

analytical_models.equation_role: Empirical saturating-exponential relation between imposed equivalent strain and dislocation density.
analytical_models.model_note: ρf = ρ0 + k1(1 − exp(−k2 ε)). For MAF-1, ε = 0.46, ρf measured = 5.57 × 10^15 m^-2.

analytical_models.equation_role: Exponential decay of grain size with imposed equivalent strain.
analytical_models.model_note: df = d0 exp(−k3 ε). For MAF-1, ε = 0.46, df measured = 35 μm.

unmapped_findings: For the MAF-1 sample the equivalent strain is reported as 0.46 in Table 1 (XRD-derived data) but as ≈0.47 in the process description text.
Average Kernel Average Misorientation (KAM) value for MAF-1 is 0.72° (MAF-0 = 0.34°), indicating significantly higher local (stored) strain after one pass.
No deformation twinning occurs in this alloy during MAF; only a negligible annealing twin boundary fraction of 0.007 is present in MAF-1.
The MAF-1 billet survived one pass without fracture; the sample could only be forged a total of five times before breaking on the sixth attempt.
The tensile specimens for MAF-1 were cut from the located region of the MAF billet (Fig. 3a) with two specimens tested per pass to confirm reliability.

FE simulation for MAF-1 predicted a maximum strain of approximately 0.6 in the central region of the specimen, exceeding the applied external equivalent strain value of 0.46, in an X-shaped deformation pattern.
